title: Merge ch-otel-demo-eks into this repo as ch-opentelemetry-demo
context: Two sibling repos overlay the same OpenTelemetry Demo 3.0.0 release and cannot be deployed together. This repo (langfuse-sample-agent-app) owns the Compose stack, four custom images tagged by content hash, and a Langfuse-traced AI shopping assistant (concierge/ + frontend/ overlay and patches). ch-otel-demo-eks owns an OpenTofu + Helm EKS deployment (Graviton, scale-to-zero, kubectl port-forward access), an in-cluster ClickStack collector writing to ClickHouse Cloud, and a session-replay frontend patch (@hyperdx/browser). Both patch package.json, pages/_app.tsx and pages/_document.tsx, and there can only be one frontend image. Outcome: one repo, one upstream pin (3.0.0 / 1755859a), one patch set, one image set, one Python CLI, two targets (laptop Compose, EKS Helm). THE FULL DESIGN IS IN .claude/plans/refactored-marinating-rain.md (target layout, argparse tree, Kubernetes Secret table, static vs generated Helm values, and the bash-to-Python behavior-preservation mapping table) AND the plan-phase verification record with its corrections is in .claude/plans/plan-claude-plans-refactored-marinating-witty-sunrise.md. READ BOTH before implementing any task. User decisions already made (do not re-open): new public repo mbarretta/ch-opentelemetry-demo with this history as the trunk and the EKS repo imported via git subtree add --prefix=deploy/eks (no squash); one unified Python CLI with the EKS bash ported to `demo.py eks ...` subcommands (tofu/helm/kubectl/aws/docker stay shell-outs, the bash and envvars.* are deleted); session replay compiled into the single frontend image and enabled on both targets whenever ClickStack is configured (SESSION_REPLAY=auto); Langfuse stays external (Langfuse Cloud) on both targets, keys in a Kubernetes Secret on EKS; upstream pin 3.0.0 everywhere so DEMO_REF=d6fd782e disappears and the replay hunks are rebased onto 3.0.0; internal identifiers (astronomy-concierge image prefix, compose project, Langfuse prompt/trace names, concierge/ package) stay. Three plan-phase decisions: core.py exposes THREE subprocess chokepoints (run, capture, popen) so images.stage() keeps streaming git archive into tarfile; task 4's rrweb-in-telemetry.jsonl assertion moved to manual post-merge validation and replaced by an automated smoke gate; the public repo is created and origin repointed BEFORE wave 1. PRE-FLIGHT, done by the orchestrator as direct commits before wave 1 dispatches (NOT harness tasks): (1) git subtree add --prefix=deploy/eks, (2) housekeeping commit — COPY (do not git mv, .claude/ is untracked in the EKS repo) feat-otel-demo-eks.json from /Users/barretta/workspace/ch/ch-otel-demo-eks/.claude/plans/ into .claude/plans/ and rebuild-index, git mv deploy/eks/LIVE-VALIDATION.md to docs/history/eks-live-validation-2026-09-09.md, git mv NATIVE_AGENT_UI_PLAN.md to docs/history/, root .gitignore gains the deploy/eks/ patterns and deploy/eks/.gitignore is removed, .dockerignore gains deploy and launcher, pyproject.toml name becomes ch-opentelemetry-demo, (3) gh repo create + git remote set-url + git push -u.
verification: scripts/dev-setup.sh && .venv/bin/ruff check concierge scripts tests launcher && .venv/bin/pytest -q && ([ ! -x scripts/check-frontend.sh ] || scripts/check-frontend.sh)
constraints: subprocess is imported and called only in launcher/core.py; every other launcher module goes through core.run(), core.capture() or core.popen()

No secret value reaches argv or disk: Kubernetes Secrets are assembled in Python and piped to `kubectl apply -f -` on stdin; ClickHouse and Langfuse auth travel in request headers or function kwargs, never a command line

Tofu identifiers var.name = "otel-demo-eks", state bucket otel-demo-eks-tfstate-<account> and state key otel-demo-eks/terraform.tfstate are unchanged — moving any of them replaces the live EKS cluster
The upstream pin stays 3.0.0 / commit 1755859a everywhere; no DEMO_REF variable and no d6fd782e reference survives the merge

Internal identifiers unchanged: astronomy-concierge image prefix, concierge/ package name, Compose project name, Langfuse prompt and trace names. Only the repo name, README, pyproject name/description and ECR repository names change

log.note: Codex plan review: round 1 returned verdict revise with 6 findings (1 critical, 3 high, 2 medium); all 6 applied, pr3 as modified. Round 2 timed out after 482s with no envelope, so the plan stands as round 1 left it (stop_reason timeout). Round 1's critical finding is the load-bearing one: task 3 originally had depends_on [] and would have been colored into wave 1, where its worktree has no launcher/ directory and the plan verification command's 'ruff check ... launcher' exits non-zero - confirmed by running it. That finding restored task 3 to wave 2.

Phase 4.5: greedy-colored 15 tasks into 6 waves (1/3/4/4/2/1) against the four conflict classes. Verified mechanically that no task sits in a wave at or before one of its dependencies, and that no two tasks in the same wave share a predicted file. Two plan-time restructurings removed real intra-wave collisions: the EKS-only-key drop moved from task 2 to task 1 so task 2 and task 4 do not both write launcher/stack.py in wave 2, and the manifest published[svc]={repository,tag,digest} schema was pinned as task 1 ac8 so task 7 (wave 3) and task 9 (wave 4) code against a written contract instead of against each other. Waves 3 and 4 both sit at the concurrency cap of 4, so task 10 lands in wave 4 purely for capacity, not for any dependency. No post_merge_build is needed: the image manifest lives under .runtime/ which is gitignored, so nothing on the base branch goes stale when task 4 changes the content tag.

Plan-phase verification corrected ten claims carried over from the design document; the four load-bearing ones are recorded here because implementers will trip on them. (1) .claude/ is untracked in ch-otel-demo-eks, so git subtree add will not import it and the pre-flight must COPY feat-otel-demo-eks.json from the sibling checkout rather than git mv it out of the subtree. (2) core.py's log/die/need/dotenv/capture/popen do not exist in demo.py today - they are new code, not extractions - and run() is not a chokepoint: nine subprocess sites bypass it. (3) demo.py:647's function-local 'from concierge.langfuse_api import PROMPTS' deliberately shadows the module-level PROMPTS; the two are different objects from different modules and must not be unified. (4) tests/test_integration_config.py:18-27 asserts only that the literal string 'sensitive' is absent from the dumped config - it does NOT assert an ${env:...}-only pattern, so task 7 writes a real credential scan rather than copying that precedent. Also: the monkeypatch surface is 12 attributes, not ~30.

tasks.why: There can be only one frontend image, so the EKS replay patch and the concierge assistant patches must become one coherent patch set on the 3.0.0 pin.
tasks.notes: The repo rule is one patch per upstream file (frontend/patches/README.md:1-5, enforced dynamically by tests/test_frontend_overlay.py:166-171), and the EKS replay patch touches five files, three of which the concierge patches already own. So fold the replay hunks INTO 0000 (package.json: keep the lint script, add @hyperdx/browser ^0.25.1), 0001 (_app.tsx: add NEXT_PUBLIC_HYPERDX_ENABLED/URL to the window.ENV typing) and 0006 (_document.tsx: destructure PUBLIC_HYPERDX_ENABLED/URL and emit NEXT_PUBLIC_HYPERDX_* in envString), and add two NEW patches: 0009 for utils/telemetry/FrontendTracer.ts (the HyperDX.init block with url NEXT_PUBLIC_HYPERDX_URL || origin + '/otlp-http', apiKey 'managed-clickstack', tracePropagationTargets [/.*/], consoleCapture, advancedNetworkCapture, the demo.synthetic_request resource attribute, plus setGlobalAttributes({ userId, 'session.id': userId }) to compensate for losing session.id on non-assistant spans in replay mode) and 0010 for package-lock.json. REGENERATE every patch from the pristine export per frontend/patches/README.md:11-27 (demo.py stage, edit under .runtime/build/src/frontend/, git -C .runtime/build diff -- <path>); never hand-merge hunks. The 0010 lock patch is the output of `npm install @hyperdx/browser@0.25.1 --package-lock-only` inside .runtime/build/src/frontend (the EKS patch's own lock hunk has 3,703 lines of drift against 3.0.0 and will not apply). In launcher/stack.py, environment() derives PUBLIC_HYPERDX_ENABLED from SESSION_REPLAY (auto = on when ClickStack is configured, true forces on, false disables); compose.native.yaml's frontend service gets `- PUBLIC_HYPERDX_ENABLED=${PUBLIC_HYPERDX_ENABLED:-}` following the existing empty-default shape of ASSISTANT_DEMO_DETAILS at compose.native.yaml:20. tasks.title: EKS aws and k8s helper modules
tasks.why: Every other EKS subcommand shells out through these two modules, so they carry the argv shapes and the no-secrets-on-argv rule for the whole port.
tasks.notes: Port deploy/eks/scripts/lib/aws.sh and lib/k8s.sh (read them from the sibling checkout at /Users/barretta/workspace/ch/ch-otel-demo-eks or from the subtree before task 3 deletes them). aws.py: aws_login (SSO), state_bucket, tf_outputs() reading `tofu output -json` ONCE per process and caching (the map output from task 3 requires -json; the old tf_out read -raw one value at a time), tf_out(name) on top of the cache, ecr_login, ecr_has_image, ng_desired/ng_status/ng_scale, scheduler_get/scheduler_set_state, purge_state_bucket. Leave ecr_image_digest to task 9. k8s.py: kubeconfig, wait_nodes_ready, ensure_namespace, secret_manifest (build the JSON/YAML Secret object in Python with base64 values) -> apply_manifest (piped to `kubectl apply -f -` on stdin), delete_secret, helm_repo_ensure, helm_upgrade_args, exec_read/exec_write for the flagd-ui file. helm_upgrade_args must produce the exact argv from the design's deploy mapping row: helm upgrade --install otel-demo open-telemetry/opentelemetry-demo --version 0.41.0 -n otel-demo -f demo-values.yaml -f values.generated.yaml --wait --timeout 20m, with the static values file first.

acceptance_criteria.text: The full verification command passes

No secret value appears in any recorded argv across the module's tests — every Secret goes through secret_manifest and apply_manifest's stdin, and the ECR password reaches `docker login --password-stdin` on stdin
tf_outputs() invokes `tofu output -json` at most once per process no matter how many callers ask, and tf_out(name) reads from that cache
secret_manifest produces a valid Secret object with base64-encoded data values and the correct namespace, and apply_manifest pipes it to `kubectl apply -f -` on stdin rather than writing a temp file
helm_upgrade_args returns the exact expected argv including both -f flags in order (static demo-values.yaml then values.generated.yaml) and --wait --timeout 20m
ng_scale is a no-op when the node group already has the requested desired size, and waits through an UPDATING status rather than returning early
ensure_namespace is idempotent (applying a namespace manifest, not `create namespace`, so a second call is not an error)
exec_write uses the temp-file-then-mv argv shape (`sh -c 'cat > F.tmp && mv F.tmp F'`) so flagd's fsnotify watch sees an inode swap

tasks.title: EKS tunnel: detached port-forward loop with pidfile lifecycle
tasks.why: The cluster is private and kubectl port-forward is the only access path, so the tunnel has to survive SSO expiry and never leak a process group.
tasks.notes: Port deploy/eks/scripts/tunnel.sh and the k8s.sh loop. The detached loop re-invokes this CLI: sys.executable scripts/demo.py eks tunnel --loop with start_new_session=True, logging to .runtime/eks/tunnel.log, re-running `aws sso login` on credential expiry and re-running `kubectl -n otel-demo port-forward --address 127.0.0.1 svc/frontend-proxy PORT:PORT`. Pidfile at .runtime/eks/tunnel.pid. Refuse to start when the pidfile names a live process or the port is already bound; clean a stale pidfile silently. Probe readiness 20 times at 1 s intervals, and count a 503 from Envoy as up (the proxy answers before the upstream is ready). stop = killpg TERM, then KILL after 5 s. status exits 0 when up, 1 when down. The --loop body must be stdlib-only (it runs as a bare subprocess with no guarantee the venv's third-party packages are importable).

acceptance_criteria.text: The full verification command passes
start refuses when the pidfile names a live process, refuses when the port is already bound, and silently removes a stale pidfile before starting
The detached child is spawned with start_new_session=True and stop() sends TERM to the process GROUP (killpg), escalating to KILL after 5 seconds
`eks tunnel status` exits 0 when the tunnel is up and 1 when it is down
The --loop code path imports only the standard library (plus launcher modules that themselves import only stdlib)
The readiness probe polls 20 times at 1 s intervals and treats a 503 from Envoy as success
The pidfile lives at .runtime/eks/tunnel.pid and the child's output goes to .runtime/eks/tunnel.log

tasks.title: Generated Helm values with the conditional Langfuse exporter
tasks.why: An otlphttp exporter with an unset ${env:LANGFUSE_BASE_URL} fails validation and CrashLoops the collector, so the Langfuse pipeline must be conditional — which a static values file cannot express.
tasks.notes: eks_values(env, published, langfuse) returns the dict written to .runtime/eks/values.generated.yaml at deploy time. Single source of truth stays in Python: reuse collector.langfuse_span_filter() and collector.assistant_route_statements() rather than restating their content. Contents: components.<svc>.imageOverride.{repository,tag} for all four services read from the manifest's published section (shape published[svc] = {repository, tag, digest}, pinned by task 1 ac8) so helm upgrade needs zero --set; env-derived plain values (agent AGENT_MODE, MCP_ENABLED, LLM_BASE_URL, LLM_MODEL, LANGFUSE_PROMPT_LABEL, LANGFUSE_PROJECT_ID, LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_URL, CLICKSTACK_TRACE_URL_TEMPLATE; frontend ASSISTANT_DEMO_DETAILS); collector processors transform/assistant_routes (trace_statements from assistant_route_statements()) and filter/langfuse (from langfuse_span_filter()); and pipeline traces/langfuse with receivers [otlp], processors [memory_limiter, transform/assistant_routes, transform/sanitize_spans, filter/langfuse, gen_ai_normalizer, batch]. When Langfuse is configured the pipeline's exporters are [otlp_http/langfuse] and exporters.otlp_http/langfuse is defined with endpoint ${env:LANGFUSE_BASE_URL}/api/public/otel and headers Authorization ${env:LANGFUSE_AUTH_HEADER} plus x-langfuse-ingestion-version '4'; when it is not, the exporter is absent entirely and the pipeline's exporters are [debug] (still a valid pipeline, mirroring the laptop's preview-only mode). The subchart's kubernetesAttributes preset only rewrites pipelines named traces|metrics|logs|profiles, so traces/langfuse is deliberately left alone. NOTE the existing secret test at tests/test_integration_config.py:18-27 only asserts `"sensitive" not in json.dumps(config)` — it does NOT assert an ${env:...}-only pattern, so write a real check here rather than copying it.

acceptance_criteria.text: The full verification command passes

exporters.otlp_http/langfuse is present if and only if Langfuse is configured; when absent, pipeline traces/langfuse still exists with exporters [debug] and the rendered config passes collector validation

No credential value appears anywhere in the yaml.safe_dump output for a fully-configured Langfuse input — every credential is a ${env:NAME} reference, asserted by scanning the dumped string for each input secret value
The traces/langfuse processors list is exactly [memory_limiter, transform/assistant_routes, transform/sanitize_spans, filter/langfuse, gen_ai_normalizer, batch] in that order
imageOverride repository and tag are emitted for all four services from the manifest's published section, and the function raises rather than emitting a partial set when a service is missing

filter/langfuse and transform/assistant_routes are built by calling collector.langfuse_span_filter() and collector.assistant_route_statements(), asserted by equality against those functions' output rather than against a copied literal
The env-derived agent and frontend overrides listed in the notes are all present with values taken from the parsed .env
otlp_http/langfuse, when present, uses endpoint ${env:LANGFUSE_BASE_URL}/api/public/otel with the Authorization and x-langfuse-ingestion-version headers

tasks.title: EKS infra: init, apply, destroy, nightly
tasks.why: These four commands own the S3 state bucket and the cluster lifecycle, where a wrong argv either orphans a paid control plane or destroys state.
tasks.notes: Port init.sh, apply.sh, destroy.sh and nightly.sh per the design's mapping table. init: need(aws, tofu, docker, git, kubectl, helm); create the state bucket idempotently (NO LocationConstraint in us-east-1 — that call fails), enable versioning and the public-access block; `tofu init` with -backend-config for bucket, key and region; ensure the helm repo; warn on blank EKS keys rather than dying. apply: refuse before init has run; run `tofu apply` interactively with stdin inherited; write kubeconfig; `kubectl get nodes`; print the next steps (build, publish, eks deploy). destroy: stop the tunnel, best-effort down, interactive `tofu destroy`; with --purge-state delete every object version AND delete marker in batches of at most 1000 keys, then the bucket, then rm -rf deploy/eks/tofu/.terraform. nightly: `aws scheduler get-schedule` as JSON, then `update-schedule` feeding back EVERY field (the API replaces the whole schedule, so any omitted field is lost), then print `get-schedule --output table`.

acceptance_criteria.text: The full verification command passes
init's bucket creation omits LocationConstraint when the region is us-east-1 and includes it otherwise, and is a no-op when the bucket already exists
init's `tofu init` argv carries -backend-config for bucket, key and region with the values from eks/config.py and the discovered account id
apply refuses with a clear message when init has not run, and never reaches tofu apply in that case
nightly's update-schedule call feeds back every field returned by get-schedule, asserted field-by-field against a recorded get-schedule fixture
destroy --purge-state deletes object versions and delete markers in batches of at most 1000 keys and deletes the bucket only after the last batch succeeds
init calls need() with aws, tofu, docker, git, kubectl and helm, and blank EKS keys produce a warning rather than an exit
apply runs tofu apply with stdin inherited so the interactive approval still works, and prints the build / publish / eks deploy next steps

tasks.title: demo.py publish: push the four images to ECR with a platform gate
tasks.why: build-frontend.sh is retired and the cluster runs arm64, so a wrong-architecture image must be refused at push time rather than discovered as a CrashLoop.
tasks.notes: Additive only: publish/record_published/require_published go into launcher/images.py, and ONLY ecr_image_digest is ADDED to launcher/eks/aws.py — task 5 already implements and tests ecr_login, so reuse it and modify nothing else in that file. Replaces build-frontend.sh: ECR login via `aws ecr get-login-password` piped to `docker login --password-stdin`; skip a service when its tag is already present in ECR unless --force; REFUSE when manifest.platform does not match tf_out('node_platform'), naming the fix (`demo.py build --platform <node_platform>`); record manifest.published[svc] = {repository, tag, digest} using the shape task 1 pinned. require_published() is the gate lifecycle.deploy calls first: it rejects a missing published section, a service missing from it, and a stale entry whose tag differs from the current build_tag().

acceptance_criteria.text: The full verification command passes
publish refuses when manifest.platform differs from tf_out('node_platform') and its message names the exact `demo.py build --platform ...` command that fixes it
The ECR password is passed to `docker login --password-stdin` on stdin and never appears in any recorded argv
A service whose tag is already in ECR is skipped, and --force pushes it anyway
manifest.published[svc] records repository, tag and digest, and publishing one service MERGES into any existing published section rather than replacing it

require_published() rejects three distinct cases with distinguishable messages: no published section at all, a service absent from it, and a service whose recorded tag is stale relative to build_tag()
The docker tag and docker push argv are exactly as expected for each of the four services against its own ECR repository URL
launcher/eks/aws.py gains only ecr_image_digest; task 9 reuses task 5's ecr_login without modifying any other function in that file

tasks.title: flagd flags and scenario --target eks
tasks.why: The demo's fault scenarios are the whole point of the walkthrough, and they must behave identically on both targets from one pure transform.
tasks.notes: Extract the scenario flag mutation in launcher/stack.py into a PURE function scenario_flags(document, name) -> document plus a thin local writer, so the laptop and EKS paths share one transform. Then flags.scenario_write_eks(name) applies the same transform through the flagd-ui exec path. VERIFIED TRAP from the design: flag.sh's defaultVariant edit does NOT control productCatalogFailure — its targeting.if always yields a variant — so the correct mutation is targeting.if[1], which the existing concierge scenario() already does. Preserve that. flags.flag(name, variant, reset) ports flag.sh: read the fsnotify-watched copy via `kubectl -n otel-demo exec deploy/flagd -c flagd-ui -- cat /app/data/demo.flagd.json`; write with the exec temp-file-then-mv shape from task 5's exec_write; validate both the flag name and the variant against the document; no-op when the flag is already set to that variant; re-read after 2 s to confirm; --reset does `rollout restart deploy/flagd` then `rollout status --timeout=120s`. Move the existing test_fault_targets_only_selected_product test onto the pure function. Do NOT touch launcher/eks/ops.py or lifecycle.py.

acceptance_criteria.text: The full verification command passes

scenario_flags is a pure function (same input document yields the same output, no I/O) and both the laptop writer and scenario_write_eks call it — asserted by comparing the two paths' resulting documents for the same scenario
scenario_flags mutates only targeting.if[1] and leaves defaultVariant untouched, with the moved test_fault_targets_only_selected_product asserting exactly that
scenario_write_eks writes through the temp-file-then-mv exec argv and re-reads the document afterward, asserting the change landed
flag() rejects an unknown flag name and an unknown variant with distinct messages, and is a no-op (no write argv recorded) when the flag already holds the requested variant
flag --reset issues `rollout restart deploy/flagd` followed by `rollout status --timeout=120s`
The flag subcommand's help notes that productCatalogFailure is scenario-controlled rather than settable directly

tasks.title: EKS ops: verify and status
tasks.why: verify is the demo's proof that one trace id reached both ClickStack and Langfuse, and status is what tells you whether the cluster is costing money right now.
tasks.notes: Port verify.sh and status.sh. verify: the same four ClickHouse SQL queries as the bash, but issued with httpx and IN-PROCESS auth (auth= kwarg or a header, never on argv — constraint 2), plus three new checks the merged repo makes possible: an agent-span count, a count of spans whose http.route matches /api/assistant/%, and one live POST /api/assistant/message through the tunnel that reports the trace id it produced. Also report collector pod status and recent logs. A zero replay-row count is REPORTED, not a failure (replay needs a real browser). status: identity, node group, node phases (only when desired > 0), pod phases counted with collections.Counter, the helm release, tunnel state, and ECR presence for all four images at the manifest tag with distinguishable 'no manifest' and 'not published' hints, plus the nightly schedule. status exits 0 whether the cluster is idle or up (it is a report, not an assertion).

acceptance_criteria.text: The full verification command passes
ClickHouse credentials are passed to httpx in-process and appear in no recorded argv, asserted by scanning every recorded call for the password
verify issues the original four queries plus the agent-span count, the /api/assistant/% route-span count, and one POST /api/assistant/message whose resulting trace id is printed
A zero session-replay row count is reported as information and does not make verify exit non-zero
status exits 0 both when the node group is scaled to zero and when the stack is up
status reports ECR presence for all four services at the manifest tag and distinguishes 'no manifest' from 'built but not published'
status counts pod phases with collections.Counter and only queries nodes when the node group's desired size is greater than zero
verify reports collector pod status and a tail of collector logs

tasks.title: EKS lifecycle: deploy, up, down
tasks.why: deploy is where a wrong ordering costs a 20-minute helm timeout or leaks credentials into a cluster that is not ready for them.
tasks.notes: Port deploy.sh, up.sh and down.sh. deploy ORDER MATTERS and is the primary AC: (1) load env and run require_published() as a gate, (2) ECR login, (3) refuse when the node group desired size is zero — this must precede ANY kubectl call, (4) run kubeconfig and ensure both namespaces from JSON manifests on stdin (idempotent), (5) apply clickstack-credentials, (6) apply the collector manifest, `rollout status --timeout=300s`, tail 40 log lines, (7) apply clickstack-otlp-token, (8) apply-or-DELETE langfuse-credentials and llm-credentials depending on whether .env carries them, (9) write .runtime/eks/values.generated.yaml, (10) helm upgrade with both -f files and zero --set, (11) start the tunnel, tolerating failure, (12) print the /, /feature/ and /loadgen/ URLs. NOTE kubeconfig itself shells out to kubectl (lib/k8s.sh:8-14 runs `kubectl config use-context`), which is why it sits at step 4 and not alongside the ECR login. up = scale the node group, wait for nodes Ready and coredns, then deploy. down = tunnel stop, `helm uninstall --ignore-not-found --wait --timeout 5m`, delete both namespaces with --timeout=300s, scale to zero; --keep skips the workload removal and only scales down. Langfuse keys are all-or-nothing, same rule as collector_config().

acceptance_criteria.text: The full verification command passes
deploy's recorded call order matches the 12 steps in the notes exactly, and the zero-node refusal is asserted to precede every kubectl invocation
deploy calls require_published() before any AWS or kubectl call and aborts on its failure

With no Langfuse keys in .env, deploy DELETES the langfuse-credentials Secret and the generated values omit the otlp_http/langfuse exporter; with them present it applies the Secret and the exporter appears
llm-credentials is applied only when API_KEY is set and deleted when it is not
The helm upgrade argv carries exactly two -f flags (static then generated) and zero --set flags
up scales the node group, waits for nodes Ready and for coredns, then runs deploy — in that order

down runs tunnel stop, helm uninstall --ignore-not-found --wait --timeout 5m, deletes both namespaces with --timeout=300s, then scales to zero; --keep skips the uninstall and namespace deletion and only scales down
A tunnel start failure at the end of deploy is tolerated (logged, deploy still succeeds) and the three URLs are printed

tasks.title: scripts/smoke.py --target eks
tasks.why: The demo's claim is one trace id landing in both ClickStack and Langfuse; smoke is the only thing that asserts it end to end on the cluster.
tasks.notes: Add --target local|eks, leaving local behavior byte-identical. On eks: drive a native assistant turn through the tunnel, then poll ClickHouse otel.otel_traces by that trace id for up to 60 s and assert the span set — services superset of {frontend-web, frontend-proxy, frontend, agent, product-catalog}, exactly one concierge.turn span, no orphan spans (every non-root span's parent is present), and http.route = /api/assistant/message on the route span. When Langfuse is configured, also GET /api/public/traces/<id> and assert the trace exists. The legacy /prompt block is skipped on eks. Reuse launcher.eks.config's load_clickstack_env / load_langfuse_env and the existing scenario() rather than re-reading .env.

acceptance_criteria.text: The full verification command passes
`smoke.py` with no --target, and with --target local, behaves exactly as before this task (no assertion changed, no step added or removed)
--target eks drives one assistant turn through the tunnel and polls otel.otel_traces by the resulting trace id for at most 60 s before failing
The eks span assertions cover all four properties: the service superset, exactly one concierge.turn, no orphan spans, and http.route = /api/assistant/message
When Langfuse is configured, --target eks also asserts GET /api/public/traces/<trace id> returns the trace; when it is not, that check is skipped rather than failed
The legacy /prompt block is skipped under --target eks and still runs under --target local
Credentials for ClickHouse and Langfuse are read through launcher.eks.config helpers and passed in-process, appearing in no argv

tasks.title: demo.py eks check: offline validation of the whole EKS surface
tasks.why: Chart processor names are verified against 0.41.0 only, so a chart bump must fail here rather than as a CrashLooping collector on a live cluster.
tasks.notes: Port check.sh and extend it. Runs with no AWS credentials and no cluster: `tofu fmt -check`, `tofu init -backend=false -input=false`, `tofu validate`; parse deploy/eks/k8s/clickstack-collector.yaml (kustomize, or kubectl --dry-run=client); then `helm template` TWICE — once with generated values that configure Langfuse and once with generated values that do not — each with example image overrides, asserting: all four imageOverride pairs landed; every processor and exporter referenced by any rendered collector pipeline is actually DEFINED in the rendered ConfigMap (this is the chart-bump tripwire); the agent Deployment carries the optional langfuse-credentials secretKeyRefs; and no chatbot Deployment exists. Missing tools are NAMED and make the command fail, not silently skipped — a check that skips is not a check. This is deliberately not part of the default pytest run (it downloads a chart); the unit tests cover the assertion logic against recorded helm template output.

acceptance_criteria.text: The full verification command passes
check runs tofu fmt -check, tofu init -backend=false -input=false and tofu validate, and parses the clickstack-collector manifest
check renders helm template twice — Langfuse configured and not configured — and asserts every processor and exporter referenced by a rendered pipeline is defined in the rendered collector ConfigMap
check asserts all four imageOverride repository/tag pairs reached the rendered Deployments, the agent carries the optional langfuse-credentials secretKeyRefs, and no chatbot Deployment is rendered
A missing tool (tofu, helm, kubectl) is named in the failure message and makes the command exit non-zero rather than skipping that check
check needs no AWS credentials and no cluster access to run, and its own tests run offline against recorded helm template output
check is reachable as `demo.py eks check` and is not invoked by the default pytest run

acceptance_criteria.text: The full verification command passes
Every command shown anywhere in README.md exists in `demo.py --help` (or a subcommand's --help) — verified by extracting the commands and checking each against the parser
The configuration table's keys match the sections in .env.example exactly, in both directions (no documented key missing from .env.example and no key in .env.example undocumented)
